content.content:
The page doesn't list a Free plan connection limit. Its other Free plan limits are:

- **Compute:** 100 CU-hours per project. Autoscaling goes up to 2 CU (8 GB RAM).
- **Autosuspend:** Compute suspends after 5 minutes of inactivity. This can't be turned off on Free.
- **Storage:** 1 GB of Postgres storage per project and 20 GB total across all projects. Object Storage includes 5 GB per project.
- **Projects:** 100.
- **Branches:** 10 per project, with no extra branches available.
- **Egress:** 5 GB of public network transfer per project.
- **History window:** 6 hours, with a 1 GB limit.
- **Snapshots:** 1 manual snapshot. Scheduled snapshots aren't available.
- **Instant restore:** Not available.
- **Auth:** Up to 60k monthly active users.
- **Functions:** 10 active and 400 waiting Capacity-Hours, plus 1M invocations, per project per month.
- **Monitoring retention:** 1 day.
- **Organization members:** Unlimited.
- **Support:** Community only.

Exceeding the storage limits blocks writes. Hitting the CU-hour or egress limits suspends compute until the next billing period. Hitting the branch limit blocks branch creation. None of these limits delete data.

content.text:
PlanetScale has no free Postgres tier, so the comparison is really Neon against Supabase. I read each vendor's pricing page today (2026-10-16). The pages were summarized by a fetch tool, not read verbatim, so check the numbers against the live pages before you rely on them.

| | **Neon Free** | **Supabase Free** | **PlanetScale** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Free tier for Postgres | Yes | Yes | **No** |
| Database storage | 1 GB per project, 20 GB total | 500 MB per database | n/a |
| Projects | 100 | 2 active | n/a |
| Compute | 100 CU-hours per project per month, autoscaling up to 2 CU (8 GB RAM) | Shared CPU, 500 MB RAM | n/a |
| Idle behavior | Suspends after 5 minutes of inactivity, and you can't turn that off | Project pauses after 1 week of inactivity | n/a |
| Egress | 5 GB per project | 5 GB, plus 5 GB cached egress | n/a |
| Branching | 10 branches per project | Not listed | n/a |
| Auth | Up to 60k monthly active users | 50k monthly active users | n/a |
| File storage | 5 GB object storage per project | 1 GB, with a 50 MB maximum upload | n/a |
| Connection limits | Not listed for Free | Not listed for Free | n/a |
| Support | Community | Not listed on the page | n/a |

**PlanetScale:** The cheapest Postgres option is PS-5 at $5/month (single node, 1/16 vCPU, 512 MiB RAM). The HA version (1 primary plus 2 replicas) is $15/month. These prices are for AWS us-east-1. The page doesn't say how much storage or transfer PS-5 includes.

**What happens at the limits:**
- **Neon:** Going over the storage limits blocks writes. Using up the CU-hours or egress suspends compute until the next billing period. Hitting the branch limit blocks new branches. Neon's page says none of these limits delete data.
- **Supabase:** Its page summary didn't say what happens when you hit a limit, so I can't tell you.

**How they differ:**
- **Neon:** It gives you more storage and far more projects. Its compute scales to zero after 5 minutes, which suits many small or intermittent projects. The free compute allowance is capped at 100 CU-hours.
- **Supabase:** It bundles auth and file storage with the database, but it has less database space and only 2 projects. Its pause comes after a week of inactivity, which is much later than Neon's 5 minutes.

**Sources:**
- Neon: https://neon.com/pricing
- Supabase: https://supabase.com/pricing
- PlanetScale: https://planetscale.com/pricing
